quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers don't see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Talk to other drivers on the road to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find a different route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you cannot cross. This is true even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes unclear.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, changes how you judge speed and distance, reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with siren and/or flashing lights approaches you, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens approaches, drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for traffic crossing, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Cancels the effect of the alcohol.
Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not reduce your blood alcohol level. While it may keep you awake, it cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require a driver to slow down and pay extra attention.

questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, such as vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow. Work zones use orange signs with black letters or symbols. Slow down and pay extra attention when driving through a work zone.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean that passing is:

options.text: Allowed only from your direction of travel.

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you will have the fewest accidents if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Match your speed to the traffic around you (if it is within the speed limit). Vehicles going the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: You must obey school crossing guards:

options.text: Unless you do not see any children present.

questions.explanation: Always watch for crossing guards near schools. You must always obey their directions.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are traveling. They may be going faster than they appear. Make sure you have enough space to change lanes safely before passing. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes before you try to pass.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Blow your horn to warn cars you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to blend in with traffic.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield to pedestrians and all traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. You should:

options.text: Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles can hide in your blind spot or be missed because they are small. Always look carefully for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, you should:

options.text: Look toward the center of the road.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their lights, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see enough of the road to stay in your lane. Do not keep your bright lights on in response.

questions.question: When may you go through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or crosswalk at any stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and go when it is safe.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?

options.text: If there is no oncoming traffic.
If the vehicle ahead is going under the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Two solid yellow lines mean neither direction can cross them, except to turn into a driveway or business entrance. You cannot pass over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash through it means something is not allowed. This sign says U-turns are not permitted.

questions.question: What happens to fines for traffic violations in construction and maintenance zones?
questions.explanation: In Oklahoma, fines for traffic violations in construction or maintenance zones are doubled when workers are present and warning signs are posted.
